samples.summary: The drift job checks out the pinned pipeline but no longer compares the vendored bytes against it — `vendor/pipeline/` is now only verified against a manifest committed in the same PR, so the "pinned, sha256-verified copy" claim is self-referential.
samples.evidence: `- run: node scripts/vendor-pipeline.mjs` (ci.yml:344) runs the OFFLINE verify path, which hashes each file against `VENDOR.json` and checks `manifest.commit === pinnedCommit()`; it accepts no `--pipeline-dir` and never reads `.pipeline-check`, which the previous step checked out at the pinned SHA (ci.yml:333-338). `verify-pipeline-drift.mjs` now only asserts non-reappearance and import targets — the byte comparison it used to perform was removed. A hand-edited vendor file with a hand-updated hash therefore passes a BLOCKING gate, which is the same silent-divergence failure mode the mirror had and that this PR's rationale cites. The pinned checkout is already on disk in that job, so re-verifying vendor content against it costs nothing.

samples.summary: The new guard only inspects `import`/`import()` specifiers, so the retained half's non-import references to the deleted mirror (data paths, workflow `node ./scripts/agent/x.mjs` invocations) are outside the gate that this change makes blocking.
samples.evidence: `mirrorImports` matches `from "…"` / `import("…")` / `import "…"` inside `scripts/agent/**` only. The three concrete breakages in this PR — agent-iterate-ci.yml's `node ./scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs`, harvest.mjs:66 and cache-report.mjs:248 — are all non-import references and all pass the gate. The job's own comment claims it asserts "nothing that stayed may import a path that no longer resolves"; extending it to `.github/workflows/*.yml` invocations and to `path.join(HERE, …)` literals is what would make that claim match the failure it is protecting against.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The iterate job's adapter (agent-iterate-ci.yml:137-149) stages the trusted pipeline into .trusted-agent, copies it to $RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools, then deletes it — it never runs the `mv .pipeline-src/packages/pipeline scripts/agent` step that agent-loop.yml:56, agent-fix.yml:73/:144, agent-rerun.yml:61/:269, agent-review-panel.yml:363/:1318 and agent-review-on-demand.yml:63 all use. So `./scripts/agent/...` resolves to the branch checkout (:106-110), where summarize-ci.mjs, metrics.mjs and set-state.mjs do not exist: `scripts/agent/*.mjs` contains none of them; scripts/agent/vendor/pipeline/ has metrics.mjs and set-state.mjs but no summarize-ci.mjs; VENDOR.json's file list omits it entirely (it exists only in the ephemeral .trusted/ runner staging dir, not an in-repo path). Nothing regenerates them (root package.json:39 postinstall only sets hooksPath; scripts/agent/package.json has no prepare/postinstall). Line :306 `DIAG="$(node ./scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs)"` has no continue-on-error and runs under the default `bash -e`, so the step and the whole iterate job fail hard. :247/:491 (metrics.mjs) and :257/:332/:454 (set-state.mjs) are continue-on-error or `|| true`, so a paged CI-fix PR silently never gets agent:blocked or its effort summary. The neighbouring loop-status steps (:271, :470) already read "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools/loop-status.mjs", confirming these invocations were missed by that migration. No guard makes it unreachable: the job runs for any managed base-repo branch (:86), and workflow_run executes the default-branch definition. Under the design-fit rubric this is a critical incomplete-migration fit violation — the CI-fix loop cannot function as the change intends.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree. harvest.mjs:64-66 defines HERE as scripts/agent and LENSES_PATH as scripts/agent/lenses/lenses.json, but that file does not exist — the only lenses.json in the tree is scripts/agent/vendor/pipeline/lenses/lenses.json, and scripts/agent/lenses/ is absent entirely. loadLensNames() (harvest.mjs:2042-2049) catches the ENOENT, logs "panelSaw will be empty" and returns [], so the harvest run proceeds. That empty list is passed from cmdHarvest (2119) through harvestPr (1627) into latestLensRuns(..., names) (1662), which at review-state.mjs:138-143 builds `want = new Set(names)` and drops every check run not in it — with [] no lens run can ever match, so every harvested record carries an empty panelSaw. Peer consumers were migrated (eval/run.mjs:752, eval/config-build.mjs:273, eval/config-hash.test.mjs:41, eval/config-build.test.mjs:30, cache-report.test.mjs:138) while this path.join was not, and I found no test or guard asserting harvest's LENSES_PATH resolves (harvest.test.mjs only contains stale scripts/agent/lenses/... strings as fixture text). Incomplete migration of a moved module leaving a fail-quiet dead path is a real, unguarded fit defect; no not-present/already-guarded ground applies.

No guard, no counterexample, and it is a spec/fit gap rather than a taste preference, so no refutation ground applies.
